northern Africa. By the 18th century,
both the French and the Italians culti-
vated eggplant, which they called
aubergine.  Thomas Jefferson introduced
the eggplant to the United States.
However, it was not until the 20th century
that Americans began to use the eggplant
as a food.  Previously, it was used as a table
decoration.  Today, the eggplant is most
popular in the cuisines of southern Italy
and the Middle East.
The eggplant is a frost-intolerant
perennial grown as an annual.  It will sus-
tain damage if the temperature falls below
65° Fahrenheit.  Eggplant is available
throughout the year.  The peak season is
from July to October.  Florida and North
Carolina produce half the domestic crop.
In the winter months, California and
Mexico are also major suppliers.
Uses
Eggplant is very perishable and should
be stored in a cool, dry place.  It can be
refrigerated in a plastic bag for 3 to 4 days.
Because it contains a heat-sensitive toxin
that can induce diarrhea and vomiting,
eggplant must be cooked before eating.
